test_title: SSC Selection Post 2025 (Matriculation Level) Official Paper (Held On: 29 Aug, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: The origin of the Ganga River is from which of the following?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Gangotri Glacier**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ganga River** originates from the **Gangotri Glacier**, which is located in the **Uttarkashi district of Uttarakhand**, India.
 
• The river emerges in the form of the **Bhagirathi River** from **Gaumukh**, a cave-like structure at the snout of the glacier.
 
• The **Bhagirathi** later converges with the **Alaknanda River** at **Devprayag**, marking the official beginning of the Ganga River.
 
• The **Gangotri Glacier** is around **30.2 kilometers long** and **2 to 4 kilometers wide**, making it one of the largest glaciers in the Himalayas.
 
• The glacier is situated at an altitude of approximately **7,100 meters above sea level**, surrounded by peaks like **Chaukhamba, Shivling, and Bhagirathi**.
 
• *Hence, the correct answer is Gangotri Glacier.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Gangotri Glacier:**

 
 
• The glacier is a primary source of water for the Ganga River, which is considered sacred in Hinduism.
 
• It is a retreating glacier, with its snout (Gaumukh) receding approximately 10 to 30 meters annually due to **climate change** and global warming.
 
 
 
• **Other Options:**
 
 
• **Siachen Glacier:** Located in the eastern Karakoram range in Ladakh, it is the largest glacier in the Indian subcontinent but does not contribute to the Ganga River.
 
• **Zemu Glacier:** Found in Sikkim, this glacier feeds the Teesta River, which flows through Sikkim and West Bengal.
 
• **Pindari Glacier:** Located in the Kumaon region of Uttarakhand, it forms the Pindar River, a tributary of the Alaknanda River.
 
 
 
• **Importance of the Ganga River:**
 
 
• The Ganga is considered the **lifeline** of millions of people in India, providing water for drinking, agriculture, and industrial use.
 
• It is revered as a **goddess** in Hindu culture and worshipped during festivals such as **Ganga Dussehra** and **Chhath Puja**.
 
• The river basin supports approximately **600 million people** and spans an area of around **861,404 square kilometers**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Conservation Efforts:**

 
 
• The **National Mission for Clean Ganga (NMCG)** was launched in 2014 under the **Namami Gange Programme** to rejuvenate the river.
 
• Efforts focus on reducing pollution levels, afforestation, and biodiversity conservation.
 
 
 
• **Religious Significance:**
 
 
• The Ganga is believed to cleanse sins and is a major site for **ritual bathing** and cremation along its ghats.
 
• Prominent pilgrimage sites along the river include **Haridwar, Varanasi, and Prayagraj**.
